notes.text: An asynchronous lookup_async (returning the stream its copy is queued on) must hold the entry's read pin until the copy has completed, not merely been queued, and record hit counters only then; the synchronous lookup, which delegates and syncs afterwards (src/lib.rs:2477-2488), inherits the same need. FR-039 step (2) states the rule for batch_lookup. Needs an interface decision (pin guard or caller-held pin); deferred with fix 7 to its separate issue.

proposals.spec_says: The `initialize` method MUST validate that the `dispatch_map` and `memory_tier` receptacles are bound before proceeding. Other receptacles are validated lazily on first use.
proposals.code_does: max_eviction_attempts / store_backpressure_ms committed only after every validation, just before `initialized` is published; a failed initialize changes neither
proposals.old_text: - **FR-012**: The `initialize` method MUST validate that the `dispatch_map` and `memory_tier` receptacles are bound before proceeding. Other receptacles are validated lazily on first use.
proposals.new_text: - **FR-012**: The `initialize` method MUST validate that the `dispatch_map` and `memory_tier` receptacles are bound before proceeding. Other receptacles are validated lazily on first use. An `initialize` that returns `Err` — an unbound required receptacle, an empty `data_pci_addrs`, or a drive-creation, partition or format error — MUST leave the dispatcher's tunables unchanged: `max_eviction_attempts` and `store_backpressure_ms` (FR-033) are committed only after every validation has passed, immediately before the dispatcher is marked initialized, so a rejected config never retunes a running dispatcher. *(Sync 2026-11-07, branch `fix/dispatcher-j33-repairs` — code authoritative, commit `11748983d`, repair DIS-INITIALIZE-FAILURE-NO-CONFIG-CHANGE, `src/lib.rs:2371-2379`. Before it both values were stored at the top of `initialize`.)*

proposals.spec_says: `read_write_stats() -> ReadWriteStats` returns aggregate read/write I/O counters (the `ReadWriteStats` type is shared from `iblock_device`).
proposals.code_does: rw_stats_baseline absorbs outgoing drives' counters before shutdown and re-initialize; read_write_stats = baseline + live drives (never decreases); interfaces doc already says Monotonic (idispatcher.rs:936-942)
proposals.old_text: - `read_write_stats() -> ReadWriteStats` returns aggregate read/write I/O counters (the `ReadWriteStats` type is shared from `iblock_device`).
proposals.new_text: - `read_write_stats() -> ReadWriteStats` returns aggregate read/write I/O counters (the `ReadWriteStats` type is shared from `iblock_device`), summed over every data drive. They are zero unless the dispatcher and its block devices are built with the `rw-telemetry` / `telemetry` features. The counters are cumulative over the dispatcher component's lifetime and MUST NOT decrease between two calls: before `shutdown` drops the data drives, and before a re-`initialize` replaces them, the outgoing drives' counters are folded into a retained baseline, and each call returns that baseline merged with the live drives. *(Sync 2026-11-07, branch `fix/dispatcher-j33-repairs` — code authoritative, commit `d65de1fef`, repair DIS-READ-WRITE-STATS-MONOTONIC, `src/lib.rs:1831-1837`, `:4595-4608`. Before it the counters read zero after `shutdown`. Known gap, tracked as A-16: a call made while the drive list is being handed over can count the outgoing drives twice, so the next call can read lower.)*
proposals.approval_note: Approved by Cornel 2026-11-07 (all proposals except gpu-services P-5; B-38 and B-45 with the options as proposed).

proposals.spec_says: `evictions_blocked_by_pin` when `IDispatchMap::try_evict_to_block` returns `ActiveReferences`, and `evictions_blocked_unpersisted` when it refuses for want of an `ssd_offset`. The call site MUST match the error variant

proposals.old_text:
causes applied, as separate counters on `TierEventStats`: `evictions_blocked_by_pin` when
`IDispatchMap::try_evict_to_block` returns `ActiveReferences`, and
`evictions_blocked_unpersisted` when it refuses for want of an `ssd_offset`. The call site MUST
match the error variant; testing `is_ok()` and incrementing a single "eviction failed" counter
does NOT satisfy this.
proposals.new_text:
causes applied, as separate counters on `TierEventStats`: `evictions_blocked_by_pin` when
`IDispatchMap::try_evict_to_block` returns `ActiveReferences`, and
`evictions_blocked_unpersisted` when it refuses for want of an `ssd_offset` (the dispatch map
answers `InvalidState` for a memory-tier entry without one). The call site MUST
match the error variant; testing `is_ok()` and incrementing a single "eviction failed" counter
does NOT satisfy this. A refusal that is neither — e.g. `KeyNotFound` for a memory-tier slot
whose dispatch-map entry is not registered yet — MUST increment **neither** counter, so that a
third cause shows up as the two counters falling short of the scanned total rather than being
absorbed into one of them. In `dispatcher` both counters are recorded by the foreground
clean-eviction scan (`evict_one_clean`); for the background evictor see FR-035.
*(Sync 2026-11-07, branch `fix/dispatcher-j33-repairs` — code authoritative, commit
`03b05d505`, `components/dispatcher/src/lib.rs:1215-1244`. Known gap, tracked as A-17:
`InvalidState` is also the answer for an entry that is not in memory-tier state, which is
still counted as unpersisted.)*

proposals.spec_says: Preserve the **drain-all-on-error** invariant of FR-054 per drive: never break early while reads are in flight; retain and report the first error per job while continuing to drain outstanding completions.
proposals.code_does: Completion::Timeout counted, submission continues, message kept; after the loop each incomplete object is failed alone; invalid tag / unexpected completion / disconnect still fail the drive
proposals.old_text: - Preserve the **drain-all-on-error** invariant of FR-054 per drive: never break early while reads are in flight; retain and report the first error per job while continuing to drain outstanding completions.
proposals.new_text: - Preserve the **drain-all-on-error** invariant of FR-054 per drive: never break early while reads are in flight; retain and report the first error per job while continuing to drain outstanding completions. A read timeout (`Completion::Timeout`) carries only the actor's operation handle, not the job tag, and the actor forgets the timed-out operation; it MUST NOT fail the drive's other jobs. Submission and draining continue, and after the loop each job whose segments did not all complete is reported `Err` with the timeout message — that job only (User Story 11 scenario 4). Completions that indicate a broken channel rather than a failed read — an invalid tag, an unexpected completion kind, a disconnected completion channel — still fail every job of that drive and stop its submissions. *(Sync 2026-11-07, branch `fix/dispatcher-j33-repairs` — code authoritative, commit `408a568d0`, `src/pipeline.rs:1402-1420`, `:1481-1495`. Before it one timeout failed every job of its drive. Known gap, tracked as A-15: the timed-out job's memory-tier slot is then released at once, although the drive may still write into it.)*

proposals.spec_says: the three MUST sum to the served count for any interval; remote_lookup_hits counted when the remote fetch succeeds — not when delivered; 002: aggregate counters MUST agree with per-entry attribution
proposals.code_does: single-key path now records lookup_hits_dram/ssd (kept through the fix-7 revert); remote hits still counted at fetch, so a failed remote delivery is ERROR but counted as a remote hit
proposals.old_text: `lookup_hits_dram` and `lookup_hits_ssd`, which with `remote_lookup_hits` **partition** every served key by route: the three MUST sum to the served count for any interval.
proposals.new_text: `lookup_hits_dram` and `lookup_hits_ssd`, which with `remote_lookup_hits` **partition** every served key by route: the three MUST sum to the served count for any interval, on both lookup paths — `batch_lookup` and the single-key `lookup`/`lookup_async` (memory-tier hit → DRAM, cold promotion → SSD, concurrent-promotion recovery → DRAM). One exception follows from counting remote hits at fetch (above): a key a peer returned whose local delivery then fails is counted in `remote_lookup_hits` but is not served (its result is `Err`, attributed `ERROR`), so over an interval with such failures the sum exceeds the served count by exactly their number. *(Sync 2026-11-07, branch `fix/dispatcher-j33-repairs` — code authoritative, commit `ec1b890ca`, repair DIS-TIER-STATS-ROUTE-PARTITION, `src/lib.rs:3434-3443`, `:3476-3490`: before it the single-key path counted `promotions_to_gpu` but no route counter. The remote-on-fetch exception is pre-existing and kept deliberately.)*

additional_edits.old_text: And `lookup_hits_dram + lookup_hits_ssd + remote_lookup_hits` MUST equal the served-key count over the same interval — the partition property, which is checkable without any knowledge of the workload.
additional_edits.new_text: And `lookup_hits_dram + lookup_hits_ssd + remote_lookup_hits` MUST equal the served-key count over the same interval, single-key lookups included, plus the number of keys a peer returned whose local delivery failed in that interval (FR-058); with no such failure it equals the served-key count exactly — the partition property, which is checkable without any knowledge of the workload.

- **FR-025**: The aggregate counters MUST agree with the per-entry attribution in the same
  responses. One deliberate exception: `remote_lookup_hits` counts a key when the peer returns it,
  so a key whose local delivery then fails is attributed `ERROR` but still counted as a remote hit
  (spec 001 FR-058). *(Sync 2026-11-07.)*

proposals.spec_says: During `initialize()`, after GPU and memory-tier are ready, the dispatcher MUST call `IGpuServices::register_host_memory` ... Registration failure MUST be logged as a warning (zero-copy pipelines require this registration).
proposals.code_does: registration runs whenever gpu_services and memory_tier are bound (no longer SPDK-gated); failure log_warn, initialize Ok; gpu-services registers with SPDK only when an SPDK env is active (CUDA-only otherwise)
proposals.old_text: Registration failure MUST be logged as a warning (zero-copy pipelines require this registration).
proposals.new_text: Registration failure MUST be logged as a warning and MUST NOT fail `initialize` (zero-copy pipelines require this registration; the DRAM path does not).
